neem.description: Neem is a hardy evergreen or semi-evergreen tree widely associated with the Indian subcontinent.
characteristics: Medium to large evergreen or semi-evergreen tree
neem.habitat: Warm tropical and subtropical environments, including dry and semi-arid regions.
ecological_importance: Contributes to vegetation cover and local ecosystem functioning
Provides habitat and resources for various organisms
Well adapted to warm and relatively dry environments
neem.biodiversity_role: Neem contributes to local plant diversity and provides ecological resources within the environments where it grows.
neem.conservation_status: Not currently considered a globally threatened species.
conservation_actions: Protect mature trees in natural and community spaces
Avoid unnecessary removal of established trees
Support native and locally appropriate vegetation
interesting_facts: Neem has a long history of traditional use in the Indian subcontinent.
Neem is well known for its ability to tolerate relatively dry conditions.
Different parts of the neem tree have been used traditionally for a variety of purposes.

tulasi.native_region: Indian subcontinent and parts of tropical Asia
tulasi.description: Tulsi, also known as holy basil, is an aromatic herb widely cultivated and associated with South Asian environments and traditions.
characteristics: Small green to purple leaves depending on variety
Small flowers arranged in elongated clusters
tulasi.habitat: Warm tropical and subtropical environments, commonly grown in gardens and household spaces.
ecological_importance: Contributes to plant diversity in cultivated and garden environments
Its flowers can provide resources for insects
Can be grown in small spaces and home gardens
tulasi.biodiversity_role: Tulsi can contribute floral resources for insects and adds plant diversity to gardens and cultivated environments.
tulasi.conservation_status: Not generally considered a globally threatened species.
conservation_actions: Maintain healthy plants in home and community gardens
Avoid unnecessary destruction of established plants
interesting_facts: Tulsi is commonly known as holy basil.
It has a long history of cultural and traditional significance in South Asia.
Its strong aroma comes from naturally occurring plant compounds.

aloe_vera.native_region: Arabian Peninsula; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions
aloe_vera.description: Aloe vera is a succulent plant recognized by its fleshy, pointed leaves and adaptation to relatively dry conditions.
characteristics: Fleshy, pointed leaves arranged in a rosette
Produces tall flower stalks under suitable conditions
aloe_vera.habitat: Dry tropical and subtropical environments, gardens, and cultivated landscapes.
ecological_importance: Contributes to plant diversity in dry and cultivated environments
Its flowers can provide resources for pollinating organisms
Adapted to environments with limited water availability
aloe_vera.biodiversity_role: Aloe vera contributes to plant diversity and can provide floral resources when flowering.
aloe_vera.conservation_status: Not generally considered a globally threatened species.
conservation_actions: Avoid unnecessary collection from natural populations
Maintain suitable habitats where native aloe species occur
interesting_facts: Aloe vera is a succulent adapted to storing water.
Its fleshy leaves help the plant survive periods of limited rainfall.
Aloe vera is widely cultivated in many parts of the world.

banyan.description: The banyan is a large fig tree known for its extensive crown and aerial roots that can develop into supporting structures.
characteristics: Broad leaves with a leathery texture
banyan.habitat: Tropical and subtropical environments, including forests, open landscapes, and urban or village spaces.
ecological_importance: Provides habitat and resources for many organisms
Fruits can serve as food for birds and other animals
Large trees can provide shade and contribute to local microhabitats
banyan.biodiversity_role: Fig trees can play an important ecological role by providing food resources and habitat for animals, particularly when fruiting.
banyan.conservation_status: Not generally considered a globally threatened species.
threats: Removal of mature trees during development
conservation_actions: Preserve trees during urban and infrastructure planning
Promote awareness of the ecological value of mature trees
interesting_facts: The banyan can develop numerous aerial roots that become additional supporting structures.
A mature banyan can occupy a large area because of its spreading growth.
The banyan is the national tree of India.

hibiscus.native_region: Tropical Asia; widely cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions
hibiscus.description: Hibiscus is a flowering shrub widely cultivated for its large and prominent flowers.
characteristics: Evergreen or semi-evergreen shrub under suitable conditions
hibiscus.habitat: Tropical and subtropical gardens, landscapes, and cultivated environments.
ecological_importance: Provides floral resources for visiting insects
Contributes to plant diversity in gardens and landscapes
Flowering plants can support local pollinator activity
hibiscus.biodiversity_role: Hibiscus can contribute floral resources to insects and increase plant diversity in cultivated landscapes.
hibiscus.conservation_status: Not generally considered a globally threatened species.
threats: Poor maintenance and unsuitable growing conditions
interesting_facts: Hibiscus flowers are known for their large and prominent appearance.
Many hibiscus varieties are cultivated as ornamental plants.
Hibiscus can attract insects and other flower-visiting organisms.

brahmi.native_region: Tropical and subtropical regions of Asia, Africa, Australia, and the Americas
brahmi.description: Water Hyssop is a small, creeping herb commonly found in wet and marshy environments and widely cultivated in parts of South Asia.
characteristics: Small white flowers with purple or yellow markings
Stems can root at the nodes
brahmi.habitat: Wetlands, marshes, riverbanks, ponds, and other moist environments.
ecological_importance: Contributes to plant diversity in wet environments
Provides vegetation cover in moist habitats
Its flowers can provide resources for visiting insects
brahmi.biodiversity_role: Water hyssop contributes to plant diversity in wet habitats and can provide floral resources for insects.
brahmi.conservation_status: Not generally considered a globally threatened species.
conservation_actions: Avoid unnecessary removal from natural habitats
interesting_facts: Water hyssop is also commonly known as Brahmi.
It is adapted to growing in wet and waterlogged environments.
Water hyssop has a long history of traditional use in South Asia.

sandalwood.native_region: Indian subcontinent and parts of Southeast Asia
sandalwood.description: Sandalwood is a small to medium-sized evergreen tree known for its fragrant heartwood and aromatic properties.
characteristics: Fragrant heartwood develops as the tree matures
sandalwood.habitat: Tropical and subtropical forests, dry woodlands, and cultivated areas with suitable conditions.
ecological_importance: Contributes to plant diversity in forest ecosystems
Provides habitat and resources for various organisms
Participates in ecological interactions with neighboring plants
sandalwood.biodiversity_role: Sandalwood contributes to forest plant diversity and provides ecological resources within its natural and cultivated habitats.
sandalwood.conservation_status: Wild populations have faced pressure from overharvesting and habitat loss.
conservation_actions: Support sustainable management of sandalwood resources
interesting_facts: Sandalwood is valued for the distinctive fragrance of its heartwood.
Sandalwood trees are traditionally associated with India and South Asia.
Santalum album is a hemiparasitic plant and obtains some resources through connections with other plants.

sunflower.description: Sunflower is a fast-growing annual plant known for its large flower heads and tall upright stems. It is widely cultivated for its seeds and as an ornamental plant.
characteristics: Tall annual herb with an upright stem
Large broad leaves with a rough texture
Large flower heads with yellow ray florets
Produces edible seeds in the central flower head
sunflower.habitat: Sunny open areas, agricultural fields, gardens, grasslands, and other well-drained environments.
ecological_importance: Provides nectar and pollen for bees and other insects
Seeds provide food for birds and other animals
Contributes to plant diversity in agricultural and garden environments
sunflower.biodiversity_role: Sunflowers provide important floral resources for pollinators and their seeds can serve as a food source for birds and other wildlife.
sunflower.conservation_status: Not generally considered a globally threatened species.
conservation_actions: Maintain sunflower plants in gardens and suitable agricultural areas
Avoid unnecessary pesticide use around flowering plants
interesting_facts: Sunflowers belong to the daisy family, Asteraceae.
The central flower head is actually made up of many individual flowers.
Sunflower seeds are widely used as food and for producing vegetable oil.
